head: bcaf7a2538a10176c89dd1fddddafbe29826b56e
scope: Basic durable publication ownership and startup recovery for full-group Finish. Private staging/lifetime flock, bound manifest and hard links before final name, Preparing/Armed/Keep/Discard, conservative unknown retention and durable diagnostics. No real hardware, production daemon, real sensors/capture, new effects, commit/push or installation.

protocol.binding: Manifest v1 binds nonce, device persistence key, full group, operation ID, original expected GroupRevision, source SHA. Entries bind kind/key/dev/inode; paths are derived. Keys/digests/schema/duplicates/record and scope budgets are validated.
protocol.publication: Candidates are created within private scope directory. Fallible observer creates and syncs a hard link from its own candidate FD, validates inode, syncs manifest atomically, then caller publishes final name without overwrite. Hard link retains inode after process death.
protocol.commit: Armed is synced before owner admission; preparation errors and known negative owner readback allow Discard. Accepted storage retains data independently of runtime error. Unknown readback/Drop persists retention notice before Keep/retirement.
protocol.recovery: Production store factory and embedded manager gate replay/catalog exposure. Existing settings+profiles redo recovery runs before receipt interpretation. Accepted and Keep retained; Preparing/Discard use identity+reference-protected rollback. Armed/Keep without receipt retain and record diagnostic; absence/eviction cannot prove noncommit.
protocol.retirement: Sync resolved state, rename to done-nonce, sync base, remove private directory, sync base. In-progress initial manifest/report temporaries and resolved retirement are idempotently collected. Live lifetime lock defers startup; unknown/corrupt/symlink/link/binding errors preserve files and prevent replay.
protocol.diagnostics: Durable recovery-report.json keeps up to 64 retention notices. Current receipt remains authoritative. Public read_group_import returns actionable unconfirmed/files-retained/no-repeat-Apply error when no receipt exists for a recorded operation.

ownership_and_journal.fixture_note: The ignored child entry point is invoked explicitly via --exact --ignored by SIGKILL parent tests; no acceptance scenario is being skipped by this marker.

crash_cases: Real SIGKILL, no Drop: private unregistered candidate, published Preparing, Discard, Armed, Keep, accepted owner commit. Fresh store removes only unaccepted unreferenced finals/staging or retains accepted/unknown files.
64 real subsequent owner commits evict original receipt: retain every old file with diagnostic; settings/profile revision unchanged by recovery.
Offline references and foreign path replacement survive cleanup; altered ownership link fingerprint/root symlink/unknown manifest/report symlink fail closed.
A manifest write failure after hard-link creation vetoes final publication.
Live unknown result and Drop keep diagnostics after normal journal retirement.
Interrupted initial scope/report write and retirement are collected idempotently; live scope is not stolen.
Embedded manager makes no HID writes when recovery fails. Actual Unix RPC/MockBackend diagnoses unconfirmed import without importing it.
Accepted journal reconciles before normal manager theme replay: brightness55/rotation90 restored; repeated readback preserves runtime generation, settings and profile revision.

nested_root_lock.symptom: SIGKILL recovery parent tests blocked beyond 60s after children had exited; isolated test process was explicitly terminated.
nested_root_lock.cause: Recovery held base directory flock and called live Journal.finish(), which opened/acquired the same flock through another file description.
nested_root_lock.fix: Recovery retires directly under its existing base lock; live finish continues to acquire the lock itself. Subsequent full crash suite and workspace passed.

remaining: Exact per-syscall crash boundary injection, fsync/ENOSPC/FD exhaustion/link/cross-filesystem/rename/hanging codec and partial cleanup cases. Logical SIGKILL stages and synthesized interrupted metadata do not prove every IO boundary.
Large media/full record/scope/report budgets, recovery work cost and contended multi-process/live-writer permutations.
Named-slot durable ownership needs a separate global-slot/receipt target binding; it is not implemented by manufacturing a full-group token.
Native abrupt desktop/daemon death, lost Finish response, pending-ID/diagnostic/error/accessibility matrix; physical acceptance remains deferred.
Windows ZIP interoperability and the rest of the core parity roadmap; additional effects remain last.
